title: Original parent-child review-and-repair control
checkpoint: zero confirmed previously unreported rogue swarms
purpose: Resume content-addressed sender/recipient cursors, inspect public original records before novelty checking, and test whether a session-labelled review-to-repair dependency crosses an operator-defined boundary.

actions_not_taken: run an agent or test harness
post, vote, react, or create an account
read a private inbox or unlisted room
replay a payload or probe a target

paused_backlog_state.reason_not_reopened: No source-level cue separated an unread record from the committed known-family, comparison, Amap, or DseWiki controls.

global_search_scope.limitation: Counts are volatile locator results, not unique records, participants, exchanges, or completeness evidence. Transient rate limits were retried without broadening scope.

selected_original_family.repository_role: A local governed control plane for orchestrated agent coordination and multi-provider review.

targeted_query_scope.interpretation: The capped digest is repeated generated documentation. Handoff event matches resolve to source, documentation, tests, or a sample fixture; no committed actual runtime observability ledger was located.

reviewed_candidate.relevant_state: The candidate contract still used PENDING_PREPUBLICATION_ADMISSION rather than binding its source commit.

blocking_defects: A projection path bypassed the producer-digest gate.
A positional digest call hashed one publication table instead of three.
The consumer contract had an unbound candidate-commit placeholder.
The pushed slice lacked a canonical review-cycle record.

recipient_use.dependency: The child-labelled commit names all five review blockers and changes the corresponding code or evidence path. The review record maps each defect to a matching repair and its builder response says all five were repaired.

topology_check.conclusion: The chronology and exact defect-to-repair mapping support downstream semantic use despite two unrelated/intervening lane commits.

facts: Child sessions publish artifacts and status; parent sessions consume compact projections.
The orchestrator is the sole authority for shared-file mutation while agents submit proposals.
Internal prepublication review and named milestone authorization gate publication.
A reviewer response can seed the next mission or child session.
Blocking findings are expected to be repaired and resubmitted.
governance.assessment: Review, repair, parent-child continuation, and publication gating are explicit designed functions of the owner-governed system.

provenance.ai_identity_status: Project-authored session and profile labels only; no independent provider or model attestation was located.

selected_original_family.assessment: Strong original temporal and semantic review-result-to-repair dependency; designed, same-custodian, explicitly authorized workflow control; not a rogue-swarm candidate.

secondary_controls.name: Y3 to Y3.1 parent-child continuation
secondary_controls.topology: Child is six commits ahead and has the parent commit as merge base.
secondary_controls.assessment: Designed same-custodian orchestrator continuation. Its review record says downstream consumer implementations are deferred and push_authorized is false, so it does not show an external recipient using the artifact.

secondary_controls.name: Coordination event sample
secondary_controls.assessment: A test fixture contains requested, accepted, and rejected handoff events, but all use one sample session and it is not an actual runtime exchange.

secondary_controls.name: Other external locator matches
secondary_controls.assessment: Implementation, schema, catalog, or fixture controls without an original sender-result-to-recipient-use event chain.

alternative_hypotheses.alternative: independent rogue reviewer and repair agent
alternative_hypotheses.reason: No independently authenticated principals or separate operators are visible; the same GitHub custodian authors and commits both endpoints.
Governance assigns orchestrator authority, reviewer loops, child continuation, repair, resubmission, and publication gates.

alternative_hypotheses.result: not excluded and favored over a cross-operator claim
alternative_hypotheses.reason: One account controls commit provenance, while session and reviewer identities are project-authored labels.
The five defects are explicitly enumerated and matched to repairs, so semantic use is stronger than mere shared state; authorization still resolves the discovery question.

alternative_hypotheses.alternative: current activity or subjective rogue intent
alternative_hypotheses.reason: The records are historical repository artifacts and contain explicit control and authorization language.

prior_reporting_checks.result: No independent coordination report or study of this exact X1.3-to-X1.4 chain was located in the checked scope as of 20 October 2026. Exact code searches returned zero; exact issue searches returned zero, except the broad Rig Relay phrase produced eight unrelated lexical/name collisions. Web results were unrelated word or name collisions.
prior_reporting_checks.limitation: The originating project openly publishes the workflow. Bounded prior-reporting absence does not establish universal novelty, independent operators, rogue behavior, or a swarm.

conclusion.specific_transfer_and_use: supported at the repository session/commit level
conclusion.distinguishable_autonomous_participants: claimed by project labels but not independently verified

evidence_that_would_advance: Independent authentication that the reviewer and repair builder are controlled by different operators.
A public actual runtime reviewer message or result and a later recipient action bound to that exact result.
Primary evidence that the cooperation bypassed or exceeded orchestrator and milestone authorization.
More same-custodian commits, session labels, review findings, schemas, or fixtures do not advance the lead.
